slides.title: Orchestration isn't automation at scale. It's *decision-making* at scale.
The pitch
slides.body:
Forty scripts, three teams, buy the orchestrator — *now you have a platform*.
Then the tool arrives.

slides.title: The real work
slides.body:
Not wiring scripts together.
*Answering questions nobody wrote down.*

slides.title: What runs first. What blocks what.
slides.body: Which steps run in parallel without *racing each other* for the same device.

slides.title: Step 6 fails after step 5 changed state
slides.body:
Roll back, hold, or wake someone up?
And *who decides* that at 2am — the tool, or a person?

slides.title: The tool discovers nothing
slides.body:
It executes the dependency graph *you hand it*.
Hand it a wrong one and you've bought a faster way to be wrong.

slides.title: The whiteboard test
slides.body:
Can't draw the order, the blockers, the rollback path?
*You're not ready to buy the tool that automates it.*

slides.title: Draw the graph before you buy the tool.
slides.body:
Automation is execution. Orchestration is judgment, encoded.
Where does your dependency graph live — a diagram, or a person?
